name: Polar Coordinates
description: Describing positions using distance and angle from a central point (center, not axes).

content.overview: Ever given someone directions like "walk 5 steps that way" while pointing? Congrats, you've already used polar coordinates. Instead of "go right 3, then up 4," you just say "go 5 units, in that direction." Distance + angle = position, done. {{viz:diagram-01}}
keyPoints: Polar = position using (r, θ), where r is distance and θ is angle
r = how far you are from the origin (the radius)
θ = which direction you're pointing (usually 0° to 360°)
Shines whenever something's circular or orbital
You can always convert back and forth between Cartesian and polar
content.whyItMatters: Circular motion, orbits, anything that spins—all of it gets way easier once you switch to polar. Problems that look painful in (x, y) often turn almost trivial once you describe them as (r, θ) instead. Learning when to make that switch is a genuine physics superpower.
